title: Expedited interop sandbox lane for high-value customer model onboarding
creator: Aisha Nordin
description: Problem: Enterprise customers occasionally request rapid onboarding of third-party or customer-provided model variants (new architectures, quantized builds, or pinned older releases). Current intake queues and eval gates prioritize safety and compatibility at the cost of long lead times (weeks). High-revenue customers have asked for a predictable, expedited path that preserves core safety/eval guarantees while enabling faster sandbox access for integration testing and early feedback.
objective: Design and operationalize an "fast-path" called the Expedited Interop Sandbox Lane (EISL) that provides high-value customers with rapid, timeboxed sandbox access to requested model variants. EISL should maintain minimal automated compatibility and safety checks, a clear sponsorship and SLO contract, and explicit rollback/deprecation clauses.
triage_flow: Customer submits model request via catalog intake form with sponsorship checkbox and justification
PM triages request within 48 hours; validates commercial sponsor and assigns to EISL if criteria met
Security/compliance quick-scan (automated) runs: license check, known bad-pattern signatures, and allowed data residency; must pass or be remediated
Automated compatibility smoke tests (API surface, tokenization, basic generation stability) run in shadow against a small reserved pool
If smoke tests pass, model is provisioned into a sandbox namespace with strict quotas and observability enabled; customer is granted access for a 14-day window
During sandbox, telemetry dashboard and nightly evaluation snapshot shared with customer; PM and SRE monitor for regressions
After 14 days, a stewarded decision: escalate to full onboarding (standard gate), extend sandbox (one-time), or sunset the variant with deprecation notice
acceptance_criteria: EISL intake checklist and form fields published in Confluence
Automated smoke test suite (API, tokenization, basic quality) passes for >= 80% of inbound models within 24h
Telemetry dashboard template with cost/latency/error breakdowns available and populated for every sandbox session
Clear sponsorship contract template and legal sign-off flow exists for enterprise customers
Pilot with 3 enterprise customers completed and lessons and metrics documented
risk_assessment: Medium-high: faster onboarding increases chance of unstable variants entering user testing. Mitigations: strict quota isolation, short sandbox windows, automated regression alerts, and mandatory sponsor acceptance of rollback/deprecation terms.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal): run EISL for two internal teams for 1 week to validate smoke tests and telemetry
Phase 1 (pilot): invite 3 sponsoring enterprise customers, limit to 2 concurrent sandboxes each
Phase 2 (scale): open EISL to additional sponsored customerswith SLA guardrails and quota automation
Phase 3 (integrate): merge successful EISL variants into standard onboarding pipeline or document deprecation path
qa_plan: Deploy smoke-test harness as a GitHub Actions workflow gated in intake pipeline
Create synthetic prompt set covering 6 common enterprise intents for nightly quality snapshots
Create chaos scenarios: throttled KV cache, single-GPU failover, and latency spike to validate graceful degradation
Run a teardown test to ensure sandboxed resources are reclaimed and cost accounting is correct
metrics_and_signals: Number of sandbox incidents requiring immediate rollback
Delta in per-token cost vs baseline for hosted catalog models
Customer satisfaction NPS for onboarding experience

What SLA do we provide during the sandbox (best-effort vs. uptime targets)?
